identity.trade: Crops and the great oak: Greenhollow's south meadows feed the vale; the Pennick farm is the largest.

greeting: Reeve here. Yes, it is as dull as it sounds. Ask anyway.
Strangers in Greenhollow get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: Everyone owes everyone a little. Nobody agrees on the sum.
The scarecrow by the north field has moved twice. The farmer says he did not touch it.
The south fields have gone violet at the edge. Only a little. Somebody says it's the light.

opinions.dacey_dobbin: Dacey lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.morning: Early start. The field has been awake an hour.

dialogue.aside: Smell the air, friend. Rain by supper. Bring a cloak, or come in.

greeting: Ale is fair, stew is hot, and I do not do credit.
You will hear Greenhollow before you see it. Ask at the Pennick Farm, Greenhollow.
rumour: Harvest crews drink the barley they cut. Somebody should tax that circle.
The cellar is cold and the cellar is empty. I ordered more. The order came back as promises.
A cart of seed went missing between the barn and the mill. No tracks.
Whatever you hear about Greenhollow, half of it is true. We argue about which half.

opinions.eorl_seedley: Eorl keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.
opinions.tuck_shaw: Tuck undercuts me. I forgive Tuck. Mostly.

time.evening: Last light. The work is done or it is dark. Both are fine.

dialogue.aside: Ah. You. Let me look at you a moment. Fine. You pass. Come in.

greeting: Bring iron or bring coin. Preferably iron.
Greenhollow is fields and the great oak. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Plough blades, sickles, hinges. Honest iron for honest mud.
The forge hums when the stones dim. Not loud. Enough to notice.
A well on the east road runs dry every dusk and fills by dawn. Nobody wants to ask why.

opinions.dacey_dobbin: Dacey undercuts me. I forgive Dacey. Mostly.

time.night: Shouldn't you be inside? The fields are quiet, but the dark has ears.

dialogue.aside: There you are. I was just thinking of you, which is rare, and a compliment.

greeting: Take your time. Touch nothing you cannot afford.
Fields do not wait for visitors, but I will spare a moment.
rumour: Seed, rope and lamp oil. The three things every farmer remembers on the last day.
Sold three lanterns today. People are afraid of the dark again.
Barn cats bring in too many rats and too few mice. Odd, that.
Ask in Greenhollow who built the Pennick Farm, Greenhollow and you will get a different name each time.

opinions.dorrit_merrow: Dorrit is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.rain: Rain. Good for the barley, bad for the knees. Bless it.

dialogue.aside: Welcome. Wipe your boots. Please. Soap is dear and floors are dearer.

greeting: You are somebody's grandchild. I can tell by the walk.
The Pennick Farm, Greenhollow is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: I remember the Long Dark. Nobody asks. Nobody wants the answer.
The old well tastes of iron this season. I do not say the stones are why.
The Great Oak hums in a storm. Gilda Pennick insists it always has.

opinions.cade_yoxall: Cade keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.morning: Early start. The field has been awake an hour.

greeting: Acorns are free. Opinions about the oak are not.
Folk come to Greenhollow for fields and the great oak. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: The oak has a new hollow. The children say a face lives in it. I told them it is a knot.
The reeve's tally says forty sacks. The barn says thirty-eight. The barn is honest.

opinions.dorrit_merrow: Dorrit works hard and talks harder.
opinions.mags_barrow: Mags knows the trade. I will say that for Mags.

time.evening: Last light. The work is done or it is dark. Both are fine.

dialogue.aside: You have a new scar, and fewer coins than last time. Sit.

greeting: Mud is honest. Walk on it.
Welcome to Greenhollow. Mind the Pennick Farm, Greenhollow. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: The field by the hedge goes quiet at dusk. No crickets. I stopped sowing there.
The hedgerows grow faster than the hedger can trim. I trimmed twice this month.

opinions.dorrit_merrow: Dorrit knows the trade. I will say that for Dorrit.

time.night: Shouldn't you be inside? The fields are quiet, but the dark has ears.

dialogue.aside: A friend is a rare coin. I have spent worse.

greeting: Rain tomorrow. My knee says so.
Harvest is the only holiday we keep. The rest is work.
rumour: Violet at the field edge, only a little. I am told it is the light.
Wolves keep to the hedge line and never cross it. As if the hedge were a wall.
A stranger asked at the Pennick Farm, Greenhollow for the oldest person in Greenhollow. We sent him to the wrong house, on purpose.

opinions.gethin_ledger: Gethin works hard and talks harder.
opinions.sorrel_tolliver: Sorrel knows the trade. I will say that for Sorrel.

time.rain: Rain. Good for the barley, bad for the knees. Bless it.

dialogue.aside: Sit. I have news. Three pieces, one of them true, I think.

greeting: Soil does not care who you are. It cares what you do on Tuesdays.
Good boots. The fields are that way.
rumour: Seed is dear and wheat is cheap. Somebody is laughing and it is not me.
Crows gather on the east field in a ring. Not feeding. Standing.

opinions.cade_yoxall: Cade knows the trade. I will say that for Cade.

time.morning: Early start. The field has been awake an hour.

dialogue.aside: Forgive me. It has been a long week and a longer day. Still, it is good to see you.

greeting: Grain is weight, flour is weight, patience is the one thing I cannot sell.
Greenhollow is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: The mice left the mill. All of them, in one night. That is not a good sign.
The wheat came up thin on the stone side and thick on the far side. Odd.
If trade slows, Greenhollow feels it first. If it speeds up, Greenhollow feels it last.

opinions.cade_yoxall: Cade works hard and talks harder.
opinions.fiske_thackeray: I would trust Fiske with a purse. A small one.

time.evening: Last light. The work is done or it is dark. Both are fine.

dialogue.aside: Hello. A pause. I am glad you came. That is all.

greeting: Hold the mule. He is not as bad as he looks.
First time in Greenhollow? The Pennick Farm, Greenhollow is the place to start.
rumour: Toll keepers keep changing. Their prices are the only thing that stays the same.
Greenhollow lives by fields and the great oak. When that fails, so do we.

opinions.gavin_farrow: Gavin works hard and talks harder.
opinions.helm_winslow: Helm knows the trade. I will say that for Helm.

time.night: Shouldn't you be inside? The fields are quiet, but the dark has ears.

dialogue.aside: My friend. Come, I kept something for you. A small thing. It means a lot to me.

greeting: Do not stand between a ewe and her lamb. She will not read the sign.
rumour: Sheep go missing near the old barrow. The shepherds do not look for them.
When Greenhollow is quiet we say it is peaceful. When it is very quiet we say nothing.

opinions.gethin_ledger: Gethin works hard and talks harder.
opinions.reda_nettle: Reda and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

time.rain: Rain. Good for the barley, bad for the knees. Bless it.

dialogue.aside: Good to see you. Now, what do you need, and what can you spare?

greeting: Timber! Well, soon. Stand back.
rumour: Fewer deer in the cut this year. Fewer birds too. The wood is holding its breath.
Ask anyone in Greenhollow about the Pennick Farm, Greenhollow. You will get four stories and one fact.

opinions.dorrit_merrow: Dorrit knows the trade. I will say that for Dorrit.
opinions.sorrel_tolliver: Sorrel works hard and talks harder.

time.morning: Early start. The field has been awake an hour.

dialogue.aside: Excuse the dust. Work does not stop for friends, though it does pause.

greeting: Mud is honest. Walk on it.
rumour: Crows are thick this year. They knew about the harvest before I did.
The Pennick Farm, Greenhollow was busy last week. Something is stirring, or somebody is.

opinions.helm_winslow: Helm knows the trade. I will say that for Helm.
opinions.milo_nettle: Milo works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Last light. The work is done or it is dark. Both are fine.

dialogue.aside: Punctual as ever, friend. I admire that. I also resent it.

greeting: I am not lost. I am exploring.
rumour: Mum says do not go past the last post. I am only going to the one before it.
The old well tastes of iron this season. I do not say the stones are why.

opinions.milo_nettle: Milo and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

greeting: Do you have a dog? I do not have a dog. Yet.
rumour: I saw a light in the hedge last night. Do not tell Mum.
Wolves keep to the hedge line and never cross it. As if the hedge were a wall.

opinions.cade_yoxall: Cade is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.

clues.note: A sack by the door has been slit and sewn back up. It is lighter than it should be.
Boot prints, one heel worn down, coming and going. They stop where the lane meets the great oak.
Someone re-inked a line of the count. The ink is newer than the page.

stashes.say: You carry four split logs from the oak-wood stack.
You shoulder four sacks of wheat.
